description:
One of the following commands: 

  - 'info'                : Print version, citation, and basic parameter overview
  - 'selftest'            : Run a short self-test to verify RAxML is working properly
  - 'parsimony'           : Compute a parsimony starting tree
  - 'jackknife'           : Perform a bootstrap/jackknife analysis
  - 'bootstrap'           : Synonym for jackknife
  - 'search'              : Perform a thorough ML tree search
  - 'evaluate'            : Compute ML estimates of branch lengths and substitution parameters on a fixed topology
  - 'append'              : Append bootstrapped trees to an ML tree
  - 'classify'            : Assign query sequences to a reference tree (experimental)
  - 'consense'            : Compute a consensus tree from a set of input trees
Name of the input multiple sequence alignment file in PHYLIP format.
Specify a file that contains multiple partitions for the alignment. The file format is described in the manual.

Initial or fixed tree file name. If you specify a tree file with -t, RAxML will not compute a parsimony starting tree, but read the tree from the file instead. This is useful for bootstrapping or when you want to evaluate a specific tree.
File containing multiple trees (e.g., bootstrap trees). Used for bootstrapping or for computing a consensus tree.
File with taxonomy information for the sequences. Used in conjunction with the classify command.
Specifies the algorithm to be executed. See the list under <command> above for available functions. Note that some functions require additional parameters.
Substitution model to use. Examples: GTRGAMMA, GTRCAT, PROTGAMMAAUTO, etc. See the manual for a complete list of available models.
If this flag is used, RAxML will treat all sites in the alignment as variable. This is useful for certain types of analyses where invariant sites should be ignored.
Number of alternative runs/analyses to perform. For example, when conducting a tree search, RAxML will perform N independent searches starting from different parsimony trees.
Generate a random starting tree using either e.g., BIONJ or PARSIMONY methods. Type can be BIONJ or PARSIMONY.
Use DNA evolutionary models (same as specifying -m GTRGAMMA for DNA).
Random seed for generating pseudorandom numbers (e.g., for bootstrapping or tree searching).
Full path to write output files. Make sure the path exists and is writable.
Name appended to result files (e.g., RAxML_result.NAME).
Specify the rate category cutoff for CAT-based models. Default is usually 10 or 20 depending on the model.
Random number seed for bootstrapping. Must be specified when doing bootstrapping (-f b or -f j).
Number of threads to use for parallelization (SMP parallelization only).
Specify the initial alpha shape parameter for the gamma distribution of rate heterogeneity across sites.
Use the KRYLOV method for optimizing branch lengths (experimental).
File specifying predefined taxon groupings (used in certain constraint-based analyses).
Specify a custom log file name to write RAxML output.
Comma-separated list of taxon names to be used as outgroup(s). The tree will be rooted at these taxa.
Random seed for randomizing stepwise addition order during parsimony tree construction.
Resume a previous run that was interrupted. RAxML will attempt to recover intermediate files and continue.
Restore a run from a checkpoint file (e.g., RAxML_checkpoint.NAME).
Number of iterations for certain algorithms (e.g., thorough search options).
Full path to write output files. Make sure the path exists and is writable.
Name appended to result files (e.g., RAxML_result.NAME).
Specify a custom log file name to write RAxML output.
Do not print bipartition support values on the ML tree (suppresses printing of bootstrap values).
Do not print confidence values on the tree (alternative to -M).
Number of threads to use for parallelization (SMP parallelization only).
Random seed for generating pseudorandom numbers (e.g., for bootstrapping or tree searching).
Random number seed for bootstrapping. Must be specified when doing bootstrapping (-f b or -f j).
Random seed for randomizing stepwise addition order during parsimony tree construction.
Specify the initial alpha shape parameter for the gamma distribution of rate heterogeneity across sites.
Specify the rate category cutoff for CAT-based models. Default is usually 10 or 20 depending on the model.
Number of iterations for certain algorithms (e.g., thorough search options).
Use the KRYLOV method for optimizing branch lengths (experimental).
Print help message and exit.
Print version information and exit.
Resume a previous run that was interrupted. RAxML will attempt to recover intermediate files and continue.
Restore a run from a checkpoint file (e.g., RAxML_checkpoint.NAME).
